title: Linear Algebra Done Wrong
byline: Sergei Treil · Brown University, 2017 edition (free online)
note: Review exercises are not broken out. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A rigorous first course in linear algebra for mathematics majors, “done wrong” in the sense that it brings in determinants early instead of avoiding them as Axler does. It moves from vector spaces and linear maps through systems of equations, rank and change of basis, to determinants, eigenvalues and diagonalization; then inner product spaces, orthogonal projection, least squares and adjoints; the spectral theorem, polar and singular value decompositions; quadratic forms and Sylvester’s law of inertia; dual spaces and tensors; and finally Cayley–Hamilton, generalized eigenspaces and the Jordan form.
